newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean students battle riot police in protest.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean students battle riot police in protest.

text.p: More than 200 South Korean students battled riot police at a university on Thursday, in a violent commemoration of a major student protest last year that collapsed under a harsh government crackdown, witnesses said.

The protestors gathered at the front gate of Yonsei University in Seoul to remember the death of student activist Roh Soo-sok. He died in March last year from a heart attack during a demonstration in downtown Seoul.
Witnesses said about 10 members of the Yonsei student government formed a human wall by holding hands to try to prevent the students from entering their campus.

In August last year, two buildings on Yonsei campus were occupied and badly damaged after almost 10 days of protests by mostly non-Yonsei students described as "pro-Pyongyang". Hundreds of students barricaded themselves in the two buildings.
The government deployed thousands of riot police and dumped liquid tear gas from helicopters to crush the movement.
Since the incident, many university students have voted for less radical students to represent their interests within the school and support for protests has dwindled.

Thursday's trouble began when police dragged some of the protesters away and fired tear gas to disperse the students, witnesses said. Radical students confronted police with blazing petrol bombs, rocks and steel bars.
Although no injuries were reported, some protesters were detained, witnesses said.
